claims: The Chicago River was dyed green for St. Patrick’s Day 2026 on Saturday, March 14, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. CDT.
Plumbers Local 130 performed the tradition of dyeing the Chicago River.
The dyeing turned the water a brilliant green for several hours between State and Columbus.
The downtown St. Patrick’s Day parade followed shortly after at noon.
The process takes about 45 minutes to an hour.
Members of the Chicago Plumbers Union use boats to spray an orange powder.
The orange powder turns brilliant green once it hits the water.
Some bridges close to spectators, according to City of Chicago information.
The 2026 celebration occurs on the Saturday nearest St. Patrick's Day
